page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-144 is a compute-optimized server instance featuring 144 vCPUs mapped to 72 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz, this x86_64 architecture platform includes a 504 MB L3 cache. The system is configured with 288 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data places this instance in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores. It also achieves top-tier results in memory bandwidth tests, reaching 543.81 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 223.72 GB/sec for write operations. Single-core performance, however, falls into the average category under stress-ng testing, though it maintains top-tier status in Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations.

The Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to top-tier performance in LLM inference prompt processing across small, medium, and large models. Despite the lack of dedicated GPU hardware, the CPU-based matrix acceleration enables 329.43 tokens/sec for medium model prompt processing. The primary hardware tradeoff is the low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2 GB per core and the complete absence of local NVMe storage, requiring external network-attached storage for persistent data.

Given its high compute density and advanced instruction support, the c4-highcpu-144 is designed for compute-bound workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, and CPU-based machine learning inference. It is also highly effective for high-throughput static web serving and database operations, where its top-tier memory bandwidth can be fully utilized. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance maximizes compute resource density per dollar for parallelizable tasks, though workloads requiring massive memory footprints or local high-speed storage may find the resource allocation unbalanced.
description: The Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-144 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor with 144 vCPUs and 288 GB of RAM. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, it provides a lean, compute-dense configuration with 2.0 GB of memory per core. Benchmarks show top-tier multi-core CPU performance, exceptional memory bandwidth, and strong cryptographic capabilities. The processor features Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512, enabling top-tier prompt processing speeds for large language models despite the absence of a GPU. However, single-core performance remains average. This server is optimized for highly parallelized, compute-heavy workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, database operations, and CPU-based machine learning inference, offering high qualitative cost efficiency for raw parallel processing at the expense of local storage and high memory-per-core ratios.
